name: Grade-Two
reason: Source term 'Grade Two' (a rank of divine artifacts) was kept nearly verbatim, hyphenated as 'Grade-Two' to fit the adaptation's weapon-grade naming convention.
description: The second-highest grade in the divine weapon ranking used in the Upper Realm, notably within the Divine Weapon Hall of the Thirteen Palaces arc (Eps 1045+). A Grade-Two Divine-Class weapon is a rare treasure that most warriors cannot hope to claim, outclassed only by Grade-One arms.

name: Hall Master
reason: The source title 'Hall Master' was carried over unchanged, as it already fits the Western fantasy register.
description: The title of the leader of a Hall, most prominently Cloud Hall. From Ep 519 onward it refers to Tia (source: Ning Yudie, the young newly installed Hall Master of Cloud Hall), whom the elders welcome and report to during the Cui Xie crisis; the title is also used for the masters of other halls later in the show.

name: Nightshard Spear
reason: The literal source weapon name 'Cold Plum Ancient Blood Spear' was condensed to the punchier 'Nightshard Spear' to fit the Western fantasy register.
description: A majestic spear wielded chiefly by Lavender in Eps 1087-1170, humming with dangerous energy as her soul recovers its power. Its source counterpart bears the words 'Ancient Blood' and is wielded outside the Wheel of Reincarnation.

name: Elder Dunn
reason: The character's Chinese name Xiao Daolai was fully localized; 'Dunn' was chosen as a short, venerable-sounding surname befitting an ancient elder, with the honorific 'Elder' replacing his 'Old Palace Master' title.
description: The former Palace Master of the Misty Cloud Palace counterpart, who ruled it for millennia and once owned the thunder sword Zane claims (Ep 1059). A would-be Heavenly Master, he gives Zane a runestone with the sword's cultivation method and has taken exactly one direct disciple in his long life — the gifted girl the Palace later confirms as his student (source: An Xin), whom others call a rare treasure.

name: Star of Golden Sand
reason: Source location 'Yellow Sand Star' (the 12th star of the middle Heaven Domain) was renamed 'Star of Golden Sand' for a more evocative Western fantasy register.
description: A desert star in the middle Heaven Domain where the Elysian Keep (source: the mini Immortal Mansion) goes to ground in Eps 1181-1212. Some twenty Supreme Lords encircle it, sweeping its surface with divine senses after concluding the Keep never left the star; their combined power could shatter the entire star in a blink.

name: Thoughtless Minds
reason: The source faction 'Gods Without Thought' was renamed 'Thoughtless Minds', preserving the no-thought concept in a more natural English phrase.
description: One of the three major factions of the human race in the late-story Upper Realm arcs (Eps 1199-1284), holding sway over thousands of worlds through strategic marriages and alliances. Its prodigies are famed in the Illusion Battlefield, though only two of its members have ever broken into the top ten; Lawson, Nigel, and Sloane stand among its leading figures.

name: Elder Apeiron
reason: The source epithet 'Indefinite Old Woman' (rendered inconsistently as 'Indefinite Old Man' in the NovelHi translation despite the character being an old granny) was localized as 'Elder Apeiron', using the Greek term for 'the boundless/indefinite' to preserve the meaning of her title.
description: An ancient and powerful old woman, master of the Indefinite Tower counterpart in the Extreme Purple Realm. In Ep 968 she takes Cora (source: Xi Youqin) as her final direct disciple after 'that old fool' finds the girl for her, brushing aside Krista's claim. She later serves as an authority on the Illusion Battlefield, explaining that every race in the universe sends its geniuses there (Eps 1066-1067).

name: Lodestone
reason: The source's 'Divine Origin Magnet Stone' was simplified to the real-world magnetic mineral 'Lodestone' for the Western fantasy register.
description: A marvel of the universe: magnetic stone fusing the Original Laws of the Five Elements (the master sheet lists seven laws, including Wind and Electricity), originating from Sacred Mount Lodestone in the Chaotic Ocean of Stars. It first appears as the blue testing stone of the pre-qualifying trial (Eps 459-461) and recurs late in the story as shield material and as a source of magnetic power that can be drawn out (Eps 904-1261).

name: Godly Way
reason: The source cultivation concept 'Divine Dao' (also rendered 'Divine Way') was localized as 'Godly Way', replacing the Chinese 'Dao' with a Western-register equivalent.
description: A supreme path of cultivation appearing in the final arcs (Eps 1234-1312): a full-fledged method of proving one's divinity, such as the Five Elements variant cultivated in the source by Ji Luoxue. Deeper comprehension of the Godly Way makes a cultivator a candidate for true godhood.

name: Holy Land
reason: The source term 'Holy Land' was carried over unchanged, as it already suits the Western fantasy register.
description: The class of supreme top-tier powers of the martial world, standing above ordinary sects alongside the Divine Kingdoms — great tenth-tier Holy Lands that only the mightiest warriors emerge from. Used throughout the show (Eps 563-1249) both for these institutions and occasionally for sacred territory, such as the Sacred Feather Sea once being the Holy Land of the Dragon-blooded.

name: Groundstone Hall
reason: Source 'Lingyun Hall' (the Misty Cloud Palace's hall for newcomers) was renamed 'Groundstone Hall', trading the Chinese name for an English one that signals the entry-level tier beneath Cloudswallow Hall.
description: The lower of the two halls of warriors in the Misty Cloud Palace arc (Eps 1045-1066): newcomers to the Heavenly Palace join Groundstone Hall, and advancement promotes them to Cloudswallow Hall (source: Swallow Cloud Hall). After Zane beats one of its warriors, the Groundstone Hall crowd knows better than to cross him.

name: Death Light
reason: The unwieldy source term 'Mysterious Underworld Deathly Ray' was condensed to the simpler 'Death Light' for the Western fantasy register.
description: The lethal radiance that pervades the cave arc of Eps 636-679 (source: Mysterious Underworld Cave). One step outside a protective dome — or beyond the shield of the Crabstone Amulet — under the Death Light means death, and even the cave's native creatures go still when it reaches full strength; it weakens on a yearly cycle, which dictates when the cave can be explored.

name: Celestial Root
reason: The source creature 'Southern Dipper Immortal Root' was shortened to 'Celestial Root', keeping the heavenly connotation while dropping the Chinese constellation reference.
description: A colossal plant monster of the deadly cave arc, its main body buried deep underground with mountain-thick roots spreading beneath the surface. In Eps 665-667 it trades cave-shaking blows with the Mad Scorpion (source: Vicious Scorpion), the clash tearing up a hurricane that strips a thousand feet of soil from the chasm's edge.

name: Sea Wyrm Sect
reason: Source 'Fish Dragon Sect' was renamed 'Sea Wyrm Sect', swapping the Chinese fish-dragon image for the Western 'wyrm' while keeping the maritime flavor.
description: A Third-Grade Sect perched on the far eastern edge of the main continent, built on a mountain overlooking the ocean (Eps 683-773). Reluctant to take in independent warriors, it shelters Zane after his rescue at sea; its sect master credits his own cunning for the sect surviving the Corrupted Divine Kingdom's rampage through The Heartlands practically untouched.

name: Bernard
reason: The character's Chinese name (source 'Senior Brother Lang') was fully localized; 'Bernard' was chosen as a hard-edged name fitting a ruthless ex-pirate crew leader, with the 'Senior Brother' honorific dropped.
description: A sharp-eyed warrior leading a five-man crew of former pirates turned sect disciples, hunting Shadow Pearls off the eastern coast (Eps 683-686). He discovers the injured Zane at the bottom of the sea, and later hunts down three girl disciples — only to watch his man Wray killed by Tessa's flying sword and to end up paralyzed with her blade at his face.

name: Robin
reason: The character's Chinese name Xi Xinghuai was fully localized to a US-origin name; 'Robin' with the stately surname 'Kensington' marks him as the patrician head of the house (source: the Xi Family Patriarch).
description: Head of House Kensington (source: Xi Xinghuai, Patriarch of the Xi Family of Void Sky City), the aristocratic house of Cora/Xi Youqin. A shrewd, quick-thinking man under heavy pressure over his daughter's marriage affair, he welcomes Zane to the estate, reins in the hot-headed Brent ('Brent, stop messing around!'), and weighs every visitor's motive in an instant (Eps 693-701).

name: Union of Seven Kingdoms
issues: Minor name drift: master sheet uses 'Union of Seven Divine Kingdoms', episodes use 'Union of Seven Kingdoms' (Ep 918) and 'Union of the Seven Kingdoms' (Ep 909), plus bare 'Union'.
reason: The source's allied 'seven Divine Kingdoms' — the human alliance that warred with the Dragon Bloodline — was formalized into the named faction 'Union of Seven Kingdoms' for the adaptation.
description: The ancient alliance of seven Divine Kingdoms that fought the Dragon-blooded; a True Dragon's breath destroyed three of them, and the four survivors endure to the present day (Eps 768-996). The Union profited immensely from plundering ancient ruins such as the sealed Sacred Feather Sea, and its kingdoms and Emperors spent ages trying — and failing — to crack the Heavenly Stellar Secret Realm.

name: War Emperor
reason: The source title 'War Emperor' (also rendered 'Battle Emperor' in the translation) was kept as-is for the ruling warrior-monarchs of the Divine Kingdoms.
description: The title of the supreme rulers of the Divine Kingdoms in the Union arc (Eps 781-873), from the founding War Emperor of the York Divine Kingdom to the reigning York himself. A War Emperor's attention is dangerous enough that even Zane avoids forcing his way past one, though Zane later sends a War Emperor flying with a single punch.

name: Young Master
reason: Generic honorific applied to many different heirs (Zane of House Lowell, the Young Master of House Hawthorne, etc.), not a distinct entity.

name: Seven Ruling Families
reason: The source's 'seven landowning households' that dominate the Eastern Domain were renamed the 'Seven Ruling Families of the Empire' to fit the adaptation's imperial framing.
description: The seven great houses that have ruled the Empire since its founding, standing at the very top of the imperial hierarchy (Eps 71-149). House Sterling is one of them; even powerful houses like Warrick and Blackwood rank beneath them, and crossing one of the Seven can crush even a talent like Zane.

name: Shadow Cloak
reason: An adaptation-coined garment name created to visually distinguish the show's invented 'Varsity' rank from 'Pledges', with no identifiable source counterpart.
description: The dark cloaks worn by full Varsity members of the sect, in contrast to the White Robes of Pledges (Eps 29-123). Spoken of with reverence by newer disciples, the cloak marks seasoned members who notice what others miss.

name: Maiden’s Peak
reason: Source 'Jade Maiden Peak' was simplified to 'Maiden’s Peak', dropping the Chinese 'Jade Maiden' idiom while keeping the peak's identity as the female disciples' home.
description: The peak of the sect reserved for its female disciples, left nearly empty because few women join the Sect (Eps 116-318). Home to disciples like Brenda — Yates's sharp-tongued cousin and Ingrid's close friend — it is famously tidy, and one standout disciple single-handedly carries it to the number-two ranking.

name: General
reason: Generic rank word used as shorthand for different entities — the Demon Generals of the trial arc (Eps 116-121, source 'Demon General') and the Flying Dragon General of Dragon's Keep (Ep 79) — not a distinct entity of its own.

name: Dawson
issues: The Ep 141 mention ('a respected man from the old days named Dawson' in Axel's parable) is an unrelated anecdotal figure folded into the same surface form; the Eps 483-484 mentions are the fighter Dawson Jones.

name: Dawson Jones
reason: The character's Chinese name Zhao Dun was fully localized to a US-origin name; 'Dawson Jones' was chosen as a plain, rugged name suiting an independent journeyman warrior.
description: An independent warrior known as the Divine Walker, famed for venturing alone into the Chaotic Ocean of Stars (source: Zhao Dun, whose 'Traceless Snowsteps' movement technique earned the epithet). He fights the opening match of the tournament against Segar Sutton of the Mysterious Luna Hall (Eps 483-484), relying on his earth-aspected defense, but Segar's black silk slices through his barrier and kills him.

name: Contemplation Picture
reason: The source term 'Visualization Diagram' (also 'Concentration Visualization Diagram') was renamed 'Contemplation Picture' to fit the Western fantasy register.
description: Meditation paintings counted among the Immortal's greatest works, earned by passing the final test of the Immortal Mansion trial (Eps 161-165). Cultivators meditate upon them to forge vastly stronger True Essence avatars; five exist in the Mansion's inheritance, and Zane sets his sights on claiming the fifth.

name: Tapestry of Sun Moon and Stars
localized_canonical: Tapestry of Sun Moon and Stars
reason: The source's 'Sun-Moon-Star Map' (the Sun-Moon-Star Visualization Diagram) was renamed 'Tapestry of Sun Moon and Stars' for a more lyrical Western fantasy register.
description: The fifth and mightiest Contemplation Picture of the Immortal Mansion's inheritance, won by Zane through the trial's final challenge (Ep ~164) and relied upon long after (through Ep 976). Its condensed power of sun, moon, and stars is an inheritance distinct from — and complementary to — body-forging arts like the Stellar Combat Body.

name: Viana
issues: Gender mismatch: the source counterpart Zhenren Tianqiong is male (m18/f0), but the episodes portray 'Saint Viana' as a woman ('her staff', 'her voice', 'Viana's bony hand'), even though Ep 171 introduces the same intervening voice as 'a man's voice'. Episode pronoun signal is correspondingly muddled (m5/f4).
reason: The source title-name 'Zhenren Tianqiong' (Perfected Person Tianqiong) was localized as 'Saint Viana', converting the Daoist 'Zhenren' honorific to 'Saint'; the gender was changed (or inconsistently rendered) in the process.
description: A saint-level elder of the Skyreach Sect who thunders in to stop Zane from executing Frey (source: Zhuge Feng), threatening that Zane will pay a hundredfold and that no one in the sect will save him (Eps 171-177). Viana attacks with a monstrous palm shadow, is stunned when Zane blocks it, demands an apology on behalf of the sect's hierarchy, and reports the impossible feat to Augustus, who initially dismisses it (Ep 189).

name: Carter
issues: Name collision: the Ep 336 mention ('House Carter', one of the five Castermere County families) is a separate entity sharing the surname, folded into this character's mentions.
reason: The character's Chinese surname Cao (source 'Deacon Cao') was localized to the common US surname 'Carter', with the 'Deacon' office rendered as 'Steward'.
description: Steward Carter, the Emberfin Lake steward of the Skyreach Sect (source: Deacon Cao, guardian of the Illusory Fish Pond). A sharp, pragmatic functionary, he avoids antagonizing the outer disciple Zane, sends reports up the chain that go unanswered (Ep 188), and decades later is demoted to a patrolling steward over Sir Kenneth's anger despite being blameless (Ep 970).
